patch_description:
This algorithm treats the supplied matrix as a genuine starting state rather than replacing it with a fixed construction. It first symmetrizes and repairs the input using targeted deletions: edges participating in the largest number of common-neighbor violations are removed first. This preserves more useful structure than deleting arbitrary edges.

After repair, it repeatedly adds only edges with no existing length-three path between their endpoints. That condition is exactly the safe edge-addition criterion for maintaining C4-freeness. Additions are selected with a degree-balancing score, favoring lower-degree endpoints and lower estimated blocking cost.

Several randomized repair trajectories are tried from the original input. The best saturated result is then improved with bounded one- and two-edge perturbations: remove structurally expensive edges, greedily refill, and retain only strictly better C4-free graphs. Every repair and refill stage explicitly checks the common-neighbor invariant.
